prior_keeper_note: 2026-08-05-neiso-83-ca1-reclass -- SUPERSEDED NOT RETRACTED at the 2026-08-09 promotion. Its recipe IS the new keeper's recipe: cc_steam_part_reclass, measured_chp_heat_rates, the neiso-caiso156 CT heat-rate meter screen, the neiso-71 per-reactor nuclear availability overlay and the neiso-72 hydro window all carry forward unchanged, because the new keeper is a re-solve of that exact recipe with ZERO scenario deltas. What is retracted is only its NUMBERS for 2025, which the neiso-91 bisect (owner decision D-88.3) established are not reproducible at any code version tested. The full genealogy behind it stands: before it 2026-08-04-neiso81-chpheatrate, before that 2026-08-03-neiso-caiso156-meter-screen, before that 2026-07-31-neiso-72-hy-window -- each superseded-not-retracted. ITS OWN PROMOTION NOTE, preserved verbatim for the record: neiso-83 (2026-08-05) arms cc_steam_part_reclass at NEISO -- a CLASSIFICATION-CORRECTNESS fix with ZERO free parameters, promoted on rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 13 [R-MEASURED] / 14 [R-ACCURATE] and explicitly NOT on a score. It is a replay_keeper re-solve of the 2026-08-04-neiso81-chpheatrate recipe with EXACTLY ONE DELTA (a programmatic diff of the two scenario blocks returns the single key cc_steam_part_reclass), scored against a SAME-HEAD ZERO-DELTA CONTROL (2026-08-05-neiso-83-control-zerodelta) rather than against the committed keeper (miso-124). THAT CONTROL CAME BACK BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed keeper -- max |class-hour delta| 0.000000 MW in all three years -- so unlike neiso-81 there is NO same-HEAD drift to decompose and every arm-B number is the mechanism. WHAT THE DEFECT WAS. EIA-860 6081 Stony Brook CA1 is the STEAM half of a 3x1 combined-cycle block. The LP carried it as a 96.0 MW standalone `oil` generator (VOM $4.50, 1.0 t-CO2/MWh, EFORd 0.10) while its three combustion-turbine siblings sat in CC_REGULAR/gas_cc (VOM $2.00, 0.43, 0.05) sharing its heat rate exactly. A combined-cycle steam turbine HAS NO COMBUSTION PATH -- it runs on HRSG exhaust, reports no CEMS stack (plant 6081 meters five units in every train year and none of them is CA1), and every MMBtu the block burns is already metered at those siblings. The model was burning distillate in a machine with no fuel of its own. WHY EIA-860'S `DFO` LABEL IS NOT THE MACHINE'S FUEL, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. EIA-923 Page 1 reports the CA row's OWN fuel split, and it tracks its CT siblings' split year by year across a 0.004 -> 0.468 swing in the block's oil share (|gap| 0.0016-0.0217, 2018-2022): the steam part inherits whatever the block burned. `DFO` on that row is a duct / legacy code. WHY IT IS NOT DOUBLE-COUNTING THE BLOCK'S FUEL. The incumbent heat rate is the eGRID PLANT-AVERAGE, whose PLNGENAN denominator already counts the steam part's own generation -- a BLOCK rate. Applying it uniformly to every block MW reproduces the block's total fuel burn by construction; the UNARMED state is the inconsistent one, charging a block-denominated rate to 209.1 MW of a 305.1 MW block and pricing the missing 96 MW off the distillate curve. Capacity is UNCHANGED (24,209.58 MW both arms) -- class, fuel, VOM, CO2 rate and EFORd move, and the heat rate does not. WHY A NEW FLAG AND NOT cc_steam_part_capacity. That mechanism only RESTORES rows the fuel map DROPS; a CARRIED row is outside its population entirely, which is why neiso-80 measured a byte-identical armed fleet and stamped it `I`. Its `fuel_type is None` gate is load-bearing (miso-125 s6 -- it is what keeps MISO 1004 Edwardsport's real 555 MW IGCC machine in COAL), so re-classing gets its own flag and its own ISO registry. cc_steam_part_capacity is NOT re-armed and its `I` is NOT re-stamped (rule 28a). LIVENESS AT TWO GRAINS (miso-126a -- a fleet-loader check alone is NOT proof): grain 1, a pre-arm fleet rebuild at THIS keeper's own ScenarioConfig moves EXACTLY ONE unit of 431 with total pmax conserved to the milli-MW; grain 2, the post-arm per-class ENERGY delta is oil -0.00231 / -0.00034 / -0.00139 TWh against CC_REGULAR +0.00220 / +0.00062 / +0.01078 TWh for 2023/24/25. A byte-identical arm would have scored INVALID, not inert. RULE 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE] PROVEN BY RUNNING IT: with the flag armed, the ERCOT (1,450), CAISO (782), PJM (1,922), MISO (1,975) and NYISO (460) fleets are byte-identical, and MISO's Edwardsport -- the one other member of the national re-class population -- stays COAL. PRE-REGISTERED IN NUMBERS BEFORE EITHER ARM SOLVED: results/calibration/PREREG-neiso83-stonybrook-ca1-2026-08-05.md.
note:
PROMOTED 2026-08-09 (session neiso-keeper-87-control, branch claude/neiso-keeper-87-control-sed8d2) ON OWNER INSTRUCTION, after the instruction's stated rationale was checked and found NOT to hold. NO SOLVE WAS RUN, no LP was constructed, no mechanism was tested, no lever opened, no matrix cell verdict minted (rule 28d), no holdout year of either tier touched. The only computation is over this bundle's own COMMITTED artifacts. 

WHAT THIS RUN IS. 2026-08-06-neiso-87-control was solved 2026-08-06 as ARM A -- the same-HEAD baseline -- of the neiso-87 Aug-2025 gas-basis A/B. It replays the 2026-08-05-neiso-83-ca1-reclass recipe with ZERO scenario deltas: a programmatic diff of the two run_config scenario blocks returns no differing key. So this promotion arms nothing and changes no mechanism; it changes only WHICH SOLVE of the standing recipe the dashboard and every downstream diagnostic session read. 

THE STATED RATIONALE DOES NOT HOLD, AND THAT IS ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. The promotion was requested on the ground that this run's fleet r is 'significantly better' than the incumbent's. Measured from the two committed run payloads' fuelRows, C4 fleet hourly dispatch correlation moves: 2023 gas r 0.919 -> 0.919 and coal 0.383 -> 0.383 (BIT-IDENTICAL); 2024 gas 0.930 -> 0.930, coal 0.481 -> 0.481 (BIT-IDENTICAL); 2025 gas 0.880 -> 0.882 with NRMSE 0.160 -> 0.158, coal 0.245 -> 0.246. That is +0.002 in r, in one year, against a r >= 0.70 floor both runs clear with room, and it sits inside the 0.918-0.931 band spanned by EVERY NEISO run ever registered. There is no material fleet-r difference. The genuinely large fleet-r move in this lane belongs to a DIFFERENT pair of runs -- the 2022 touchpoint, where the neiso-86 gas-basis repair took gas r from 0.809 to 0.880 -- and that is a validation-tier run that can never be a keeper (rule 16). 

THE REASON THAT DOES HOLD, and the one this promotion actually rests on: THE SUPERSEDED KEEPER BUNDLE IS A NON-REPRODUCIBLE OUTLIER. The neiso-91 bisect (owner decision D-88.3) replayed the neiso-83 2025 recipe at its own sha f8f803dd and at HEAD c710d17e -- 373 commits apart, same data root -- and got byte-identical class_hourly / system / storage / reserve_family and 0 of 8,760 hours of price difference, refuting neiso-87 section 4.0's own 'the cause is in the commit range' premise. Five candidates were eliminated by measurement (code, content-addressed inputs, solver version -- this bundle ran highspy 1.14.0, the superseded keeper's own -- cross-year LP warm-start, and a missing gitignored hydro-plant-modes partition). Four independent solves across three code versions, two chain lengths and both warm-start settings agree WITH ONE ANOTHER TO THE BIT and all differ from the committed neiso-83 bundle by the identical 731-hour January-2025 pattern. The committed bundle is the outlier and the residual cause is solve-time state it does not record. This keeper is on the reproducible side of that split. 

THE MEASURED DELTA, from the two bundles' own hourly sidecars (scored pass P2; P1 identical in direction and magnitude). 2023: 0 of 43,800 zone-hours differ, 0 classes move, mean lambda 38.4902 unchanged. 2024: 0 of 43,800 zone-hours differ, 0 classes move, mean lambda 43.7081 unchanged. 2025: 3,655 of 43,800 zone-hours differ (731 hours x 5 zones, every one in January), mean lambda 70.0868 -> 69.7524, max |dlambda| 25.5244 $/MWh; per-class energy oil -0.0773 TWh against CC_REGULAR +0.0710 / CT_PEAKER +0.0044 TWh, total generation conserved to +0.0007 TWh. On the scored criteria the 2025 row moves C3a +3.0% -> +2.5%, C2 gas +2.6% -> +2.8%, C4 gas r 0.880 -> 0.882; 2023 and 2024 do not move at all. Both directions are reported: C3a and C4 improve marginally, C2 degrades marginally, and none of it changes a single criterion's status.
disposition_note:
DETERMINATION CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS, verified IDENTICAL rather than merely compatible: 0 FAILs, the same 1 ledgered caveat (C3c price tail / scarcity, RT hourly), the same C1 headline (all 12/12, free 8/8), the same grade summary (scored 8, target-grade 7, commercial-grade 0, ledgered 1) -- criterion for criterion identical to the superseded 2026-08-05-neiso-83-ca1-reclass keeper. RULE 22 D-5(b) SATISFIED AND NOT MERELY ASSERTED: the re-verified determination is NOT worse, so this promotion proceeds without an owner escalation, and calibration-complete.json's NEISO entry is re-keyed in the same commit. NO NEW CAVEAT SLOT IS SPENT and the 2026-07-11 frontier declaration is untouched (C3c bit-unchanged: model 0 hours > $300/MWh in both runs, all three years). 

TWO DEFECTS IN THIS KEEPER ARE DISCLOSED IN ADVANCE OF ANY SESSION FINDING THEM, because the promotion was made on instruction rather than on the merits of this run against a fully-current one. 

(i) IT CARRIES A SUPERSEDED MEASURED INPUT -- a rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] regression, bounded to one month of one year. As arm A of the Aug-2025 basis A/B this run was DELIBERATELY solved on the stale NEISO,2025,8 gas-basis row (+0.04, an interpolation adopted when no measured figure existed). HEAD carries the measured -0.38 (ISO-NE Massachusetts natural-gas index, August-2025 recap published 2025-10-02, $2.53/MMBtu in both the table and the narrative), committed by neiso-87 itself. The size of the miss is measured, not estimated: arm B of that same A/B -- identical in every other respect -- gives August-2025 mean lambda 43.7004 against this run's 47.4254 (-3.7250) and 2025 annual mean lambda 69.3990 against this run's 69.7149 (-0.3160). So a fully-current re-solve of this same recipe is the run that SHOULD hold this slot, and it is the neiso-91 log's own standing recommendation (expected 2025 mean lambda 69.399). Arm B was never committed or registered, and producing it needs a solve, which this session did not run. THIS IS AN OPEN ITEM, NOT A CLOSED ONE: the next NEISO session that solves should re-solve this recipe at HEAD across 2023-2025, register it, and re-key this shard to it. 

(ii) ITS C8 EVIDENCE WAS PRODUCED AT PROMOTION, NOT AT REGISTRATION. The bundle was registered without legitimacy_diagnostics.json, so C8 forced-energy share scored SKIPPED -- an unscored PROTECTIVE criterion, which would have been a determination regression against the superseded keeper's C8 PASS. It was generated in the promotion session by scripts/legitimacy_diagnostics.py --bundle results/calibration/neiso87_control_A --iso NEISO --years 2023 2024 2025, reading this bundle's own committed artifacts and its committed run payload, with floors reconstructed via run_year(fleet_only=True) -- NO LP SOLVE. C8 then PASSES on its own data: every material class is inside its rule 20 [R-FORCED-BUDGET] cap in every year, the largest material forced share being CC_REGULAR 0.0039 / 0.0082 / 0.0074 against a 0.30 limit, and the three over-cap rows (COAL 0.337 in 2023, CT_PEAKER 0.224 in 2023, ST_GAS 0.245 in 2025) are all immaterial classes below the 2 %-of-load gating floor. D-4 off-window binding PASSES on every floor-year row (offwindow_twh 0.0 throughout). D-5 parity, D-9 overlay quarantine and D-10 free-class rescore all PASS. The bundle's metrics.json was rewritten from the same scorer (calibration_verdict.py --write-metrics) so the committed artifact and the live verdict agree. D-1 diurnal shape carries the SAME class-level gate failures the lane has carried throughout (COAL_BIT off-peak CV in all three years, 2023 ST_GAS profile r, 2025 CT_PEAKER off-peak CV); the standalone C7 gate that scored them was RETIRED at rubric v3.1 (owner amendment 2026-08-06), and they do not reach C8's grounded-above-budget escalation because no material class is above its cap. 

(iii) CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED from the superseded keeper and still true: CC_CHP sits UNDER actual in every year where it sat over -- a real, ungated and currently unclosable residual whose only named route is CLOSED WITH EVIDENCE by neiso-71 -- and the 2025 C1 CC rows stay SKIPPED on the preliminary EIA-923 vintage (13/30 CC_REGULAR and 3/7 CC_CHP prior plants missing, 57 % reporting). The neiso-83 open root-cause issue also carries forward unchanged and unfixed, since the recipe is unchanged: campd-unit-outages-NEISO.csv routes plant 6081's DIESEL peakers to plant_group=CC_REGULAR because `oil` carries no plant_group at all, derating a fully-available CC block on outages of machines that are not in it. 

(iv) NEISO IS STILL THE ONLY ISO OF SIX RUNNING THE ARCHIVED P2 COMMITMENT PASS -- this bundle's meta.json carries commitment=true and persists passes P1 and P2, and it is scored on P2, exactly as the superseded keeper was. The neiso-84 escalation (replay_keeper re-injects a recipe's flags from meta.json AFTER the --enable-legacy-p2 gate runs on parsed CLI args) is NEITHER resolved NOR worsened here and remains open for the owner. Resolving it needs a re-solve, which this session did not run; it should be settled in the same session that closes defect (i).
